steps.raw_response:
Carolyn’s reasoning state:

After that warm invitation, I felt like we were finally building something real. She said yes, she seemed glad to be included, and I left that conversation feeling hopeful. But then everything goes back to normal at the bank, and normal means polite, cooperative, distant. She doesn’t mean to be cold, I think. She’s still professional, still friendly in a careful way. But the openness we had outside of work doesn’t seem to carry over.

What I’m perceiving now is a wall that I can’t quite see through. Every conversation stays on task. Every interaction feels cordial but contained. I keep waiting for that same warmth to show up at work, but it doesn’t. So I start to wonder if I misread things, or if she’s only comfortable being close when we’re not in these roles. That lingering professional formality bothers me, not because she’s being unkind, but because it makes me feel like we’re still just coworkers after everything we shared.

That’s what shifts my intention. I don’t want to nag her or create tension. I just want to name what I feel instead of letting it sit there. I need to know whether this distance is about our work dynamic or about something she’s not saying. So I decide to bring it up directly, because ignoring it is starting to drain the trust I thought we were building.
